Recommend games on the steam summer sell

I might add more later but these are some personal recommendations just off the top of my head:

Age of Mythology - RTS - Might just be nostlagia factor but this is one of my favourite RTS games on Steam. Has great diversity in the factions and playstyles making it a lot of fun.

Portal 2 - Puzzle - You'd be hard pressed to find anybody who doesn't like it. The co-op mode is the true test of your friendship with another human being.

Arma 2/OA - MilSim - Big open world, an absolute ton of weapons, vehicles, and aircraft. This game is hit or miss, some people absolutely adore it, others hate it. If you ever played Operation Flashpoint, it's basically that but better. Also, the modding community in this game is absolutely fantastic, you can get new factions, maps, and weapons, and a lot of them are at such a high standard, they are on par with BI's actual DLC.

Hotline Miami - Top Down Action - Hyper-violent pixel art game, has an incredible soundtrack which really fits the mood. Also, while it is quite difficult, it never feels unfair. There are never any moments, in my experience at least, where you get frustrated at the game due to it bugging out or the AI cheating as you get in some difficult games.

Killing Floor - FPS - A great game to mess around in with friends, and it avoids getting repetitive due to it's great map variety. Killing Floor 2 was recently released and is the pretty much the same formula, therefore I advise trying the first one just so you know if you wanna put the money down for it.

Seconding the vote for Hotline Miami, as well as the sequel! I wrote this small review for the original, but it applies just as well to the sequel:

"Hotline Miami is the best worst trip of your life. The nightmare begins in a dingy 1989 Miami apartment, as you listen to the first in a long line of mysterious messages left on your answering machine. For whatever reason, you feel compelled to do as you're told, a task that usually involves brutally murdering dozens of armed gunmen with hair triggers. Pressing on in a search for answers only further blurs the lines between reality and rampant psychosis, and you're left wondering which possibility is the least horrifying. Vigilante gone overboard? Contract killer? Maybe you're just a delivery driver losing himself in increasingly improbable power fantasies. Maybe it doesn't matter. Maybe you don't care.

The game presents an impressive array of weapons and animal masks, each augmenting your abilities or changing the gameplay in some way. It's more of a twitchy, reflex-based puzzler than a mindless rampage, and a single misstep will lead to a messy death at the hands of your adrenaline-fueled enemies. However, any feelings of frustration that might arise are quickly washed away in a tsunami of 16bit blood and gore, and the fast-paced, addictive gameplay will have you hitting the 'retry' button out of pure reflex.

The soundtrack fits the game like a glass slipper, ghosts of acid-washed synthesizers and contemporary electronica comprising one of the best video game soundtracks you'll ever hear."

You said it better than I ever could!

The only thing I would add, is that people should be aware that Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, was a little more buggy than the first. Not to a game-breaking extent or anything, just a few minor issues with the AI being confused by walls sometimes haha.

Space Rangers HD

This is a top down "simultaneous turn" rpg/strategy game. The universe is being invaded by the Dominators and pirates are going batshit taking advantage of the situation. You get thrust in the middle of it and your goal is to unite the universe under either the pirates or the "good guys." By simultaneous turn I mean when in space you for instance direct your ship to fly to point x and shoot certain weapons at various targets. You end your turn and the enemy carries out their orders which are executed in unison. It's a fun and heavily strategic system.

The cool part about the game is how challenging and open ended it is while still having a very explicit goal. One of the achievements for the game is to beat the game without ever destroying another ship! You can trade, search planets, destroy any other ship (or base), engage in piracy, take control of space stations, and much more.

Is Small Claims Court Worth It? Article Example + Discussion Thread

This is my concern from reading the article: "In most jurisdictions, If the person won’t pay you back, you have to be your own investigator — and find out where they work and how to garnish their wages. All of which requires more money. It is easy to spend more than you are owed trying to collect."

Can Voat share their experiences, good and bad, with small claims court?

If you are owed/damaged less than $10,000 is it even worth suing? What about if you are harmed by a deadbeat?

The best asset to carry with you into small-claims as a litigant is patience, the second is a sense of humor. Two steps forward, one step back is normal when fumbling through the court system. Judges know this for pro se and will rarely permanently penalize you for trying your best to present the proper documentation, notices, etc. Keep plugging! Other than blowing a statue of limitations, most mistakes aren't fatal. It's only a matter of your time, the value of which is the cost-benefit analysis each litigant must evaluate.

For collections, supplemental proceedings (discovery of assets) are merely part 2 of the claims process, no more or less difficult than the initial complaint filing. Most courts now have online small-claims guides and fillable pdf forms that alleviates a lot of the guesswork. Assistant court clerks will usually give some measure of assistance dotting I's and crossing T's even if their initial pat response to every questions is: "We don't give legal advice." Ask nicely, they usually respond to "please".

In the linked story, the $2,700 judgment is well worth a few more hours of time and research for most people. If it is, be persistent and you'll get there eventually. If not, write it off, put it out of mind, and go have a margarita.
